I can analyse how visual and persuasive techniques are used in an advertisement poster to communicate a message and influence an audience.

Greetings from The Gaudium School!

"Education is not just about learning facts; it is about developing the ability to think, explore, and grow."

At The Gaudium School, we are committed to nurturing curious, confident, and lifelong learners. As part of this commitment, we encourage our students to participate in prestigious external examinations that provide opportunities to challenge themselves beyond the regular classroom curriculum.

· Science Olympiad Foundation (SOF) Olympiads 
· LogIQids 
· Spell Bee 
· National Astronomy & Science Olympiad (NASO) 
· International Science Olympiad Competition of Southeast Asia (ISOCSEA) 
· Singapore Asian School Math Olympiad (SASMO) 
· Harvard Undergraduate Science Olympiad (HUSO)

Why should students participate? 
· These examinations offer students an excellent platform to: 
· Strengthen their conceptual understanding of subjects. 
· Develop critical thinking, logical reasoning, and problem-solving skills. 
· Build confidence by competing at national and international levels. • Enhance analytical and application-based learning. 
· Gain exposure to competitive examinations from an early age. 
· Inspire a passion for learning while equipping students for future academic excellence.

We encourage all eligible students to take advantage of these opportunities and participate in the examinations. Such experiences not only complement classroom learning but also help students discover and realize their true potential.

notifications.detail:
Madhavi Vinod has posted the following discussion in IB MYP English (MYP Year 1) E:

Exposition(beginning): Medusa (Example)
Long ago, in ancient Greece, there lived a beautiful young woman named Medusa. She had long, shining golden hair and was admired by everyone who saw her. Medusa served as a priestess in the magnificent Temple of Athena, the wise goddess of wisdom and warfare. The temple stood on a rocky hill overlooking the sparkling blue sea, surrounded by olive trees and marble statues.
The temple was a peaceful and sacred place where silence and respect were expected. Medusa spent her days caring for the temple and offering prayers to Athena. Although she was kind and hardworking, many people spoke more about her beauty than her kindness. Her beauty became famous across the land, attracting both admiration and jealousy.
Little did Medusa know that her peaceful life was about to change forever because of the actions of powerful gods.
 
Story Mapping – Exposition(beginning)
Story Element    Details from the Exposition
Title    Medusa
Characters Introduced    Medusa, Athena (mentioned)
Main Character    Medusa
Setting (Where?)    Temple of Athena in ancient Greece
Setting (When?)    Long ago, in ancient Greek times
    Peaceful, sacred, mysterious
Background Information    Medusa is a beautiful priestess who serves Athena faithfully.
Conflict Introduced?    No direct conflict yet, but hints that something important will happen.
Descriptive Language    "shining golden hair," "sparkling blue sea," "rocky hill," "magnificent temple," "marble statues"

Pandora's Box – Exposition (MYP-1)
Long ago, when gods and humans shared the world, the mighty god Zeus decided to create a young woman named Pandora. The gods gifted her many wonderful qualities. Aphrodite gave her beauty, Athena taught her useful skills, Hermes gave her curiosity and cleverness, and the other gods presented her with special talents. Because she received gifts from every god, she was named Pandora, which means "all-gifted."
Pandora lived in a peaceful home with her husband, Epimetheus, in a beautiful valley surrounded by green hills, colourful flowers, and sparkling rivers. On the day they began their new life together, Zeus gave Pandora a beautifully decorated golden box. It was covered with intricate carvings and tied with a shining ribbon.
Zeus gave Pandora one important warning.
"Never open this box, no matter how curious you become."
Pandora admired the mysterious box every day. She wondered what was hidden inside it and why she was forbidden to open it. Although she tried to ignore her curiosity, the unopened box seemed to whisper its secrets to her.
Little did Pandora know that one decision would change the lives of all humanity forever.
Create a mapping for the exposition given above.

discussions.detail:
Exposition(beginning): Medusa (Example)
Long ago, in ancient Greece, there lived a beautiful young woman named Medusa. She had long, shining golden hair and was admired by everyone who saw her. Medusa served as a priestess in the magnificent Temple of Athena, the wise goddess of wisdom and warfare. The temple stood on a rocky hill overlooking the sparkling blue sea, surrounded by olive trees and marble statues.
The temple was a peaceful and sacred place where silence and respect were expected. Medusa spent her days caring for the temple and offering prayers to Athena. Although she was kind and hardworking, many people spoke more about her beauty than her kindness. Her beauty became famous across the land, attracting both admiration and jealousy.
Little did Medusa know that her peaceful life was about to change forever because of the actions of powerful gods.
 
Story Mapping – Exposition(beginning)
Story Element    Details from the Exposition
Title    Medusa
Characters Introduced    Medusa, Athena (mentioned)
Main Character    Medusa
Setting (Where?)    Temple of Athena in ancient Greece
Setting (When?)    Long ago, in ancient Greek times
    Peaceful, sacred, mysterious
Background Information    Medusa is a beautiful priestess who serves Athena faithfully.
Conflict Introduced?    No direct conflict yet, but hints that something important will happen.
Descriptive Language    "shining golden hair," "sparkling blue sea," "rocky hill," "magnificent temple," "marble statues"

Pandora's Box – Exposition (MYP-1)
Long ago, when gods and humans shared the world, the mighty god Zeus decided to create a young woman named Pandora. The gods gifted her many wonderful qualities. Aphrodite gave her beauty, Athena taught her useful skills, Hermes gave her curiosity and cleverness, and the other gods presented her with special talents. Because she received gifts from every god, she was named Pandora, which means "all-gifted."
Pandora lived in a peaceful home with her husband, Epimetheus, in a beautiful valley surrounded by green hills, colourful flowers, and sparkling rivers. On the day they began their new life together, Zeus gave Pandora a beautifully decorated golden box. It was covered with intricate carvings and tied with a shining ribbon.
Zeus gave Pandora one important warning.
"Never open this box, no matter how curious you become."
Pandora admired the mysterious box every day. She wondered what was hidden inside it and why she was forbidden to open it. Although she tried to ignore her curiosity, the unopened box seemed to whisper its secrets to her.
Little did Pandora know that one decision would change the lives of all humanity forever.

Long ago, in ancient Greece, there lived a beautiful young woman named Medusa. She had long, shining golden hair and was admired by everyone who saw her. The temple stood on a rocky hill overlooking the sparkling blue sea, surrounded by olive trees and marble statues.

Pandora's Box – Exposition (MYP-1)
Long ago, when gods and humans shared the world, the mighty god Zeus decided to create a young woman named Pandora. The gods gifted her many wonderful qualities. Aphrodite gave her beauty, Athena taught her useful skills, Hermes gave her curiosity and cleverness, and the other gods presented her with special talents. Because she received gifts from every god, she was named Pandora, which means "all-gifted."
Pandora lived in a peaceful home with her husband, Epimetheus, in a beautiful valley surrounded by green hills, colourful flowers, and sparkling rivers. On the day they began their new life together, Zeus gave Pandora a beautifully decorated golden box. It was covered with intricate carvings and tied with a shining ribbon.
Zeus gave Pandora one important warning.
"Never open this box, no matter how curious you become."
Pandora admired the mysterious box every day. She wondered what was hidden inside it and why she was forbidden to open it. Although she tried to ignore her curiosity, the unopened box seemed to whisper its secrets to her.
Little did Pandora know that one decision would change the lives of all humanity forever.
